 BREAKING NEWS Nov. 19, 2026, 9:51 PM UTC Donald Trump Donald Trump Trump posthumously pardons MLB all-time hits leader Pete Rose
 The baseball great, who died in 2024, pleaded guilty to federal tax evasion charges in 1990 and had been banned from the sport for betting on games. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Cincinnati Reds Pete Rose in 1974. John Iacono / Sports Illustrated via Getty Images file Share Add NBC News to Google By Dareh Gregorian President Donald Trump announced on social media Thursday that he has pardoned the late Pete Rose , baseball’s all-time hits leader.

 Slide 1 of 1 Rose, he added, “was treated terribly by Major League Baseball in not allowing him to go into the Baseball Hall of Fame.”
 Rose died in 2024. He pleaded guilty to federal tax evasion charges in 1990, and had banned for life from baseball after he gambled on his own team as a player and manager. That ban was lifted last year at Trump’s urging.
